attachments.insertion_landmark: medial base of patella, via quadriceps tendon

actions: distal oblique fibers (VMO) stabilize patellar tracking, resisting lateral subluxation

functional_compartments.name: Vastus medialis longus (proximal, oblique ~15-18deg pennation)
functional_compartments.source: Lieb FJ, Perry J (1968) J Bone Joint Surg Am 50(8):1535-1548 -- original description dividing vastus medialis into proximal VML and distal VMO; Castanov V et al. (2019) Clin Anat 32(4):515-523 -- quantitative pennation-angle confirmation of the VML/VMO architectural distinction

functional_compartments.name: Vastus medialis obliquus (VMO, distal, ~50-55deg pennation)
functional_compartments.innervation_branch: femoral n., distal muscular twig (documented separate terminal branch)

neuromuscular_junction_zone.location_description: mid-belly endplate band, short highly-pennate fibers

functional_compartments.function_note: Documented distinct, more horizontally/obliquely-pennate distal compartment; clinically important for patellofemoral tracking (VMO weakness/atrophy is implicated in patellofemoral pain syndrome).
functional_compartments.source: Lieb FJ, Perry J (1968) J Bone Joint Surg Am 50(8):1535-1548 -- original description dividing vastus medialis into proximal VML and distal VMO; Castanov V et al. (2019) Clin Anat 32(4):515-523 -- quantitative pennation-angle confirmation of the VML/VMO architectural distinction

motor_endplate_zones.method: modified Sihler's whole-mount nerve staining, 20 specimens, cross-validated with ultrasound-guided cadaveric dye injection
motor_endplate_zones.notes: Muscle divided into 10 equal-length areas along the ASIS-to-patella line; intramuscular nerve distribution was densest in areas 6-9 (50-90%), corresponding to the distal, obliquely-pennate VMO compartment recorded here. Ultrasound-guided injections targeting areas 6-9 in two fresh cadavers were confirmed on dissection to deliver dye along the muscle fibers in the intended region.
motor_endplate_zones.source: Yi KH, Hu H, Hwang SO, Ahn H, Lee JH, Lee HJ (2024) Surg Radiol Anat 46(12):2067-2073, doi:10.1007/s00276-024-03482-y -- retrieved via PubMed

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Ward SR, Eng CM, Smallwood LH, Lieber RL (2009) Clin Orthop Relat Res 467:1074-1082; Lieb FJ, Perry J (1968) J Bone Joint Surg Am 50(8):1535-1548; Castanov V et al. (2019) Clin Anat 32(4):515-523

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Anteromedial distal thigh, along the ASIS-to-base-of-patella line, over the distal 50-90% segment of that line (the VMO compartment) where intramuscular nerve density is greatest.
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: VMO is identified as the more obliquely/horizontally oriented, more distal and superficial fiber bundle of vastus medialis, distinct from the more vertically oriented proximal VML.
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: Ultrasound-guided injections in two fresh cadavers targeting this region were verified by dissection to deposit dye accurately along the densely-innervated muscle fibers.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Yi KH, Hu H, Hwang SO, Ahn H, Lee JH, Lee HJ (2024) Surg Radiol Anat 46(12):2067-2073, doi:10.1007/s00276-024-03482-y -- retrieved via PubMed
